3.20.7.en: As for the righteous desiring death, since they [dig for it as for treasures], Elijah confirms this to me in the words: "It is enough; now, O LORD, take away my life; for I am not better than my fathers" (1 Kgs 4:19).

3.20.8.en: Paul also agreed with this when the disciples at Caesarea wanted to prevent him from going up to Jerusalem, for he said: "What mean ye to weep and to break mine heart? for I am ready not to be bound only, but also to die at Jerusalem (Acts 13:21).

3.20.9.en: Father Hesychius of Jerusalem * Those who live in pleasures dread death, but the sorrowful beseech it that they may depart quickly.

3.20.10.en: The rich dread death, and the poor desire it that they may rest from their toils.

3.20.11.en: The strong tremble when they remember it, and the sick look to it in hope that they may rest from their pains.

3.20.12.en: Father Aphrahat * When the good are afflicted with evils and the wicked with good things, this is perhaps for the benefit of the good, that they may receive punishment (discipline) here if they have sinned in anything, so that they may be freed completely from eternal judgment. And the wicked find good things here that offer them deliverance in this life, so that they may be drawn on to the full torments to come. Therefore it was said to the rich man as he burned in hell: "Son, remember that thou in thy lifetime receivedst thy good things, and likewise Lazarus evil things" (Lk 16:25)... The saints walk in greater dread, fearing the luxury of this world more than its dangers.

3.20.14.en: * As for rest, what do we find in the world except constant war with Satan, and a struggle in an unceasing battle against his arrows and swords?! Our war is waged against the love of money, pride, anger and vainglory, and our struggle is constant against bodily lusts and the allurements of the world.

3.20.15.en: The mind of man is besieged by the enemy on every side, and the assaults of Satan close in upon it from every quarter. With effort the mind is able to defend itself, and scarcely can it resist in every spot. If it despises the love of money, lusts rise up within it. If it overcomes lusts, vainglory springs forth. If it triumphs over vainglory, anger and pride are kindled in it, and drunkenness with wine allures it, and envy tears apart its harmony with others, and jealousy corrupts its friendships.

3.20.16.en: Thus every day the soul suffers many persecutions such as these, and great dangers such as these distress the heart; and yet the heart still rejoices to remain here so long amid the wars of Satan! Though it would have been more fitting for our longings and desires to be set on hastening to go to Christ by way of a speedy death. For the Lord Himself taught us, saying: "Verily, verily, I say unto you, That ye shall weep and lament, but the world shall rejoice: and ye shall be sorrowful, but your sorrow shall be turned into joy" (Jn 20:16).

3.20.17.en: Which of us does not wish to be without sorrow?!

3.20.18.en: Which of us does not long to hasten to obtain joy?!

3.20.19.en: The Lord Himself also declared the time when our sorrow would be turned into joy, saying: [But I will see you again, and your heart shall rejoice, and your joy no man taketh from you] (Jn 20:16). Since our joy lies in seeing Christ... what blindness afflicts our mind, and what folly assails us, when we love the sorrows of the world, its tribulations and its tears more than hastening toward the joy that will not be taken from us?!

3.20.20.en: * What a benefit we gain by departing from this world!

3.20.21.en: The disciples grieved when Christ announced to them that He would depart, so He said to them: "If ye loved me, ye would rejoice, because I said, I go unto the Father" (Jn 28:14), teaching us to rejoice, and not to grieve, when one of our loved ones departs from this world, truly remembering the saying of the blessed Apostle Paul: "For to me to live is Christ, and to die is gain" (Phil 21:1).

3.20.22.en: We count death the greatest gain, a thing we cannot acquire by the nets of this world or reap by the sins and vices of the flesh. For by death we leave painful toils and are delivered from the poisonous fangs of Satan, to go to Christ's calling of us, rejoicing in eternal salvation.

3.21.0.en: St. Cyprian the Martyr Which wait for death, but it is not, and dig for it more than for hid treasures [21]

3.21.1.en: By saying, "dig for it more than for hid treasures," he reveals his readiness to spend every possibility in searching for death as one who searches for the greatest treasure he could possess.

3.21.2.en: Job never thought of suicide, despite his seeking death at any cost, for his life is in the hand of his God; it is not for him to end it himself.

3.21.3.en: *Those who seek mortification perfectly search for it like those who dig for hidden treasures; the nearer they come to their goal, the greater zeal they show in the work.

3.21.5.en: * The death of the righteous has become a sleep; rather, it has become life.

3.21.6.en: St. Basil the Great St. Gregory of Nazianzus looked to his elder sister, St. Gorgonia, as a living model of the Christian, and was deeply moved by her, being enamored of her piety and godliness. And he showed how she prepared for death without fear, but rather longed for it:

3.21.7.en: * Gorgonia's homeland was the Jerusalem above (Heb 22:12, 23)... where Christ dwells, and with Him the assembly and church of the firstborn, who are written in heaven...

3.21.8.en: * Everything she was able to wrest from the ruler of this world she deposited in faithful places. She left nothing behind her except her body. She parted with everything for the sake of the heavenly hope. The only wealth she left to her children is the imitation of her example, and that they enjoy what she deserved.

3.21.9.en: * Here I speak of her death and what distinguished her at that time, that I may give her her due... She longed greatly for the time of her dissolution, for she knew Him who had called her, and she preferred to be with Christ more than anything else on earth (Phil 23:1).

3.21.10.en: This saint yearned to be freed from the bonds of the body and to escape the mire of this world in which we live. And what is still more excellent, she had tasted the beauty of her Beloved, Christ, for she was constantly contemplating Him.

3.21.11.en: She knew beforehand the hour of her departure from this world, which doubled her joy. It seems that God informed her of it so that she might prepare and not be disturbed then.

3.21.12.en: She spent all her life washing herself from sin and striving to attain perfection. She received the gift of continual renewal by the Holy Spirit and became steadfast in it according to the merit of her earlier life..

3.21.13.en: Nor did she neglect to supplicate for her husband too, that he might attain perfection, and God answered her petition, for she wished that everything connected with her should be in the state of perfection that God desires of us, so that nothing on her part might be lacking before Christ.

3.21.14.en: And when the end came she delivered her testament to her husband, her children and her friends, as was to be expected from such a saint who loved all.

3.21.15.en: Her last day on earth was a day of solemn celebration; and we do not say that she died full of the days of the sons of men, for this was not her wish, since she knew that those days which are according to the flesh are evil days, and are nothing but dust and mirage. Rather she was full of the days of God... And so she was set free, or rather it is better to say that she was taken to her God, or fled, or changed her dwelling, or hastily delivered up her trust.

3.21.16.en: At the time of her repose a solemn silence fell, as though her death were a kind of religious ceremony.

3.21.17.en: Her body lay as though paralyzed after the spirit had left it, motionless.

3.21.18.en: But her spiritual father, who was watching her closely during this wonderful scene, sensed her murmuring and listened stealthily, and behold, he heard her reciting the words of the Psalmist: [I will both lay me down in peace, and sleep] (Ps 8:4). Blessed is he who falls asleep with these words in his mouth.

3.21.19.en: Thus you sang, O fairest among women, and the song became reality. You entered into sweet peace after suffering, and you reposed as befits a woman beloved of God, who lived and fell asleep amid words of goodness.

3.21.20.en: How precious is your portion! It surpasses what the eye can see, amid a host of angels and heavenly powers; it is full of splendor, purity and perfection!

3.21.21.en: Beyond all this is her vision of the Holy Trinity, which is no longer beyond comprehension and perception, which were formerly limited, held captive by the body.

3.21.22.en: I hope that your spirit will accept this praise from me, as I did for my brother Caesarius. For I was careful to pronounce eulogies for my brothers.

3.21.23.en: St. Gregory of Nazianzus * Death, for those who understand it, is immortality; but for the foolish who do not understand it, it is death.

3.21.24.en: We ought not to fear this death, but to fear the perishing of the soul, which is ignorance of God. This is what truly terrifies the soul!

3.21.25.en: * It is impossible for us to escape death by any means. Since the wise truly know this, they practice the virtues and think upon the love of God, and face death without sighs or fear or tears, considering that death is inevitable on the one hand, and on the other that it frees us from the sicknesses to which we are subject in this life.

3.22.0.en: St. Anthony the Great Which rejoice exceedingly, and are glad, when they can find the grave? [22].

3.22.1.en: *Thus Paul regarded those disciples as dead and as buried in the tomb of contemplation, those to whom he said: "For ye are dead, and your life is hid with Christ in God" (Col 3:3). He who seeks death rejoices when he finds the grave, for he who desires mortification rejoices all the more when he finds the rest of contemplation; for in dying to the world he hides and conceals himself in the bosom of inner love from all the disturbances of outward things.

3.23.0.en: To a man whose way is hid, and whom God hath hedged in [23].

3.23.1.en: He had no hope of improving his state; he saw no door of escape, nor any road to walk, since God had hedged him in, so that he became as one in his place, unable to move. As it is said in Hosea: "Behold, I will hedge up thy way with thorns, and make a wall, that she shall not find her paths" (Hos 2:6). And as Jeremiah cried out: "He hath inclosed my ways with hewn stone, he hath made my paths crooked" (Lam 3:9).

3.23.2.en: * Even death entered as a fruit of sin, and yet the loftiness of God, His tenderness and His surpassing providence turned this to the benefit of our race. What burden does death carry, tell me? Is it not a freedom from troubles? Is not death a freedom from cares? Do you not hear Job praising it in the words: Death is a help for man, a hidden way.

3.23.3.en: St. John Chrysostom * "Whose way is hid" means that he will not know when or by what means his departure from here will be. For God hides this knowledge from him; that is, He does not permit him to know, so that men may await death all their days. And thus they prepare. God hides this for our great benefit, to give us the opportunity to fulfill what He commanded His disciples: "Watch therefore: for ye know not what hour your Lord doth come" (Mt 42:24).

3.23.4.en: Father Hesychius of Jerusalem *Dear beloved brethren... We must take into consideration that we are looking forward until God wills for us to leave the world, for we now live as guests and strangers.

3.23.5.en: Let us love the day appointed for us, on which we are freed from the snares of the world and return to Paradise and the Kingdom...

3.23.6.en: For what man placed in a foreign land does not wish to hasten his return to his own country? And which of those who hasten to return (by sea) to their friends does not long for a fair wind so that they may quickly meet those who are dear to them?!

3.23.7.en: We look to Paradise as our homeland... and to the Fathers (the Patriarchs) as our fathers; why then do we not hasten, nay run, to behold our city and greet our fathers?! For we have very many dear ones waiting for us. Therefore what happiness will flood us and them when we gather together?!

3.23.8.en: What joy there is in the heavenly Kingdom, where we no longer fear death?! And what sweet, lasting happiness in eternal life?!

3.23.9.en: There is the glorious fellowship with the Apostles; there is the choir of the rejoicing prophets; there are the countless multitudes of martyrs, crowned with victory in their struggle against the passions; there are the triumphant multitudes of virgins who conquered the lusts of the flesh by their chastity... there are the merciful, crowned, those who wrought righteousness by feeding the poor and helping them, and who kept the commandments of the Lord and turned their earthly possessions into heavenly treasures.

3.23.10.en: Then let us hasten to these beloved brethren with great longing. May we desire to be with them and hasten to come to Christ.

3.23.11.en: May God look upon our great longing, and may Christ the Lord look upon the aim of our mind and our faith, He who gives the great reward that is for His glory to those who have a great desire to honor Him.

3.24.0.en: St. Cyprian the Martyr For my groaning comes like my bread, and like the waters my sighing is poured out [24]

3.24.1.en: Job's groaning became the necessary daily bread, without which he cannot live. His sorrows recur regularly, as if they were meals on which he feeds. His sighs became like a full river overflowing with sorrows without ceasing.

3.24.2.en: * If all creation is to be dissolved and the fashion of this world is to change, why should we marvel, being part of creation, that we feel a severe, general pain and are given over to sorrows that our God allows to come upon us according to the measure of our strength, and He does not suffer us to be tempted above that we are able, but with the temptation gives the way out, that we may be able to bear it?

3.24.3.en: * The Lord commands: [All things have measures and weights] (Wis 11:21), and He brings upon us trials that do not exceed our power of endurance; rather He tries with sorrow all who fight on the way of true religion, and does not allow them to be tried beyond what they can bear. He gives tears to drink in great measure (Ps 80:5) to all who ought to show that in the midst of their sorrows they keep their thanks to Him.

3.24.4.en: * I am convinced that if there is a voice that moves the good God, He will not make His mercy far off, but will give with the temptation the way out, that you may be able to bear it.

3.25.0.en: St. Basil the Great For I greatly feared a fear and it came to me, and that which I dreaded came upon me [25].

3.25.1.en: It seems that in the days of his prosperity he feared that disasters would befall him, so he says: "I greatly feared a fear and it came to me, and that which I dreaded came upon me" [25].

3.25.2.en: * As long as I am here, as long as I am in this world, as long as I bear a mortal body, as long as I sigh amid the maladies of disobedience, as long as, while standing, I am "in fear lest I fall," as long as my goodness and my evils are threatened with instability, the whole life of man together is vanity.

3.25.3.en: St. Augustine * If the hope of Christians were confined to the limits of this life, our lot would truly be bitter, for it would be confined in the body before the time (the time of eternity); but if they have the love of God and their souls withdraw from the bonds of the body, they count that the beginning of true life. Why then do you grieve like those who have no hope? So take your rest and do not fall under your troubles, but show yourself higher than the troubles and exalted above them.

3.25.4.en: * Beloved, is the trial hard? Let us endure hardships, for no one who avoids the spears and the dust of the battle wins the crown. Is the enemy deceiving you, and is his war without profit...?

3.25.5.en: * These trials are wearying, because they serve the Lord. They are weak, because the Lord has mingled their evil with weakness. But let us beware of crying out loudly because of a little pain. By this we would be condemned. For you deprive yourselves of the eternal reward given to the righteous.

3.25.6.en: You are the sons of those who confessed Christ. You are the sons of the martyrs. They resisted unto blood against sin. Therefore keep such examples near and dear to you, that you may become courageous for the sake of your Christianity.

3.25.7.en: None among us has had his flesh cut by the lash... None of us has suffered the confiscation of his dwelling... We have not been driven into exile, we have not been imprisoned... Then how great is the suffering we have endured?... In truth perhaps we should regard the source of our pain as being that we have suffered nothing, and that we are unworthy of the sufferings of Christ.

3.26.0.en: St. Basil the Great I was not at ease, nor did I dwell, nor did I rest, and the wrath (anger) has come [26].

3.26.1.en: He goes back in memory to before the trial to see that he was not at ease, for he feared that a disaster would befall him; yet this did not drive him to complacency or idleness, but he worked watchfully with earnestness.

3.26.2.en: * The unwary man who enjoys prosperity, rules over his enemies, and is praised and admired by them, needs pity more than any other man. In truth, since he expects no change, he cannot face even the problems of prosperity with propriety. So when hard times come upon him he is confused and discouraged because of his lack of caution and because he is impractical. Job, on the contrary, was not like this; even in his prosperity he expected hard times every day... Another says: "In the time of plenty think of the time of hunger: and in the days of riches think upon poverty and need." (Sir 18:25).

3.26.3.en: St. John Chrysostom * What Job grieved over was not the things his friends imagined; rather his soul was in another dread, not knowing whether the enemy was robbing him of his inner wealth, whether he had been able to plunder from him the good things, a stripping that is counted the greatest calamity. For this Job testified openly: [I was not at ease, nor did I dwell, nor did I rest, and the wrath has come upon me] [26]. He did not know peace, for he was troubled because of his children. [He was not in tranquility (quietness)], since he offered sacrifices for them every day (Job 5:1). The wrath (indignation) came upon him, for he lost his sons at one time, and his wealth and his bodily health. For even when the righteous man is very righteous, if he is pleasing to God in all things, it is impossible for him to live without coming to know the trials in this world (Jas 2:1). He cannot exist without knowing the sorrow of this world, even as the Lord said to His apostles (Jn 6:16-22). Paul himself says: "Yea, and all that will live godly in Christ Jesus shall suffer persecution" (2 Tim 12:3).. And Christ for His part said: "Be of good cheer; I have overcome the world" (Jn 33:16). Again He said: [He that endureth to the end shall live] (cf. Mt 22:10; 23:24), by the power of the Father and the Son and the Holy Spirit.

3.26.4.en: Father Hesychius of Jerusalem The desire for death no longer arises from fleeing tribulation and trials. For the true Christian, as a living member joined to the Head, Jesus Christ, receives the marks of the crucified Christ who accepted death by His own will, and so loves suffering, seeks it and desires it even unto death, not for the sake of suffering in itself, nor as an escape from the world, but because it is the sign of the fellowship of true love and the union between the suffering, crucified Bridegroom and His bride. Thus the cross, with suffering as with death, for the true believer has gone forth from being the sign of sin and the indication of man's veiling and deprivation from God, the source of happiness, to become a sign of love and fellowship. So the Apostle Paul says: "Always bearing about in the body the dying of the Lord Jesus" (2 Cor 10:4). And he affirms that these are the sufferings of Christ: "For as the sufferings of Christ abound in us, so our consolation also aboundeth by Christ" (2 Cor 5:1).

3.26.5.en: * When He stretched out His hands on the cross He cast down the prince of the power of the air, that worketh in the children of disobedience (Eph 2:2), preparing for us the way to the heavens.

3.26.6.en: * When His body was lifted up on high, the things that are in heaven appeared.

3.26.7.en: * After the bodily resurrection of our Savior, there was no longer any reason to fear death. Those who believe in Christ trample on death as if it were nothing, preferring rather to die than to deny faith in Christ. For they are convinced that death does not mean destruction but life; through the resurrection they become incorruptible...

3.26.8.en: The clear proof of this is that before faith in Christ people looked on death as a terrifying matter, as something that made them cowards. But as soon as they received the faith and the teaching of Christ, they on the contrary came to count death a small thing which they trample on, and which makes them witnesses to the resurrection which the Savior accomplished against death.

3.26.9.en: St. Athanasius the Apostolic * After Christ came and died for the life of the world, death is no longer called death but sleep and repose.

3.26.10.en: * Do you not know how the cross has set right many errors? Did it not shatter death, wipe out sin, end the power of Satan, and satisfy the being of our good body? Has it not set right the whole world, and yet you do not trust in it?

3.26.11.en: *Who can utter the mighty acts of the LORD? (Ps 2:105) Out of death we have become immortal; have you understood the victory and the way it was reached? Learn how this victory was won without toil and sweat. Our weapons were not stained with blood, nor did we stand in the battle line, nor were we wounded, nor did we see the battle, yet we have won the battle. The struggle is that of our Christ, and the crown of victory is ours.

3.26.12.en: Since the victory is ours, it befits us as soldiers to chant today with joyful voices the hymns of victory. Let us praise our Lord, saying: [Death is swallowed up in victory. O death, where is thy victory? O grave, where is thy sting?] (1 Cor 54:15-55).

3.26.14.en: Let me die, that I may live with You!

3.26.15.en: * I see in every newborn child a living image of my own birth; he is born to cry out as he enters the world, as though he had come out into the valley of tears!

3.26.16.en: Who of mankind does not bear a yoke?

3.26.17.en: Righteous Job cursed the day of his birth, and Jeremiah cried out: "Woe is me, my mother, that thou hast borne me."

3.26.18.en: And the Psalmist groans, saying: [Wherefore hast thou made all men in vain?] (b)

3.26.19.en: If these were the cries of godly men of God, then what shall I say? And with what shall I speak?

3.26.20.en: * We were driven out of the joyful Paradise, and became as those in the darkness of a night that does not pass.

3.26.21.en: Our hope has been cut off that the light of day will dawn upon us.

3.26.22.en: Our days have become full of groaning.

3.26.23.en: We often cry out with righteous Job:

3.26.24.en: Why did we not die while still in the womb?

3.26.25.en: Why did we not give up the ghost as soon as we were born?

3.26.26.en: * Thank You, O wondrous Sun of Righteousness!

3.26.27.en: You rose upon those sitting in darkness.

3.26.28.en: Nay, You came down to our earth and shared our sufferings.

3.26.29.en: Now, while You Yourself are tempted, You help those who are tempted!

3.26.30.en: Let me bear the cross, since You have borne it!

3.26.31.en: Let me accept shame, and be cast out of the camp, that I may find You there crucified between two thieves, numbered among the transgressors, You who alone are the Holy One!

3.26.32.en: Sufferings delight me as long as You are with me, and the tomb becomes heaven for me, since You have dwelt in it!

3.26.33.en: * Let me die, that I may live with You.

3.26.34.en: Now in You my soul rests!

3.26.35.en: You are my happiness and the joy of my heart.

3.26.36.en: You are my joy, my peace and my treasure!
